key_insight: A randomized controlled trial at ICLR 2025 shows that LLM-generated feedback given to reviewers makes reviews measurably more informative and increases reviewer–author engagement.
problem_solved: Addresses inconsistent, time-constrained, and uneven-quality peer reviews by providing scalable, targeted feedback to reviewers that improves review content and author response rates.
method: Randomized controlled study at a major conference (ICLR 2025): reviewers were randomly assigned to receive LLM-generated feedback suggestions or not.
LLM produced actionable feedback and rewrite suggestions which reviewers could accept, edit, or ignore; outcomes were measured on review informativeness and subsequent author engagement.
Quantitative analysis compared intervention vs control on metrics like information content, helpfulness ratings, and reviewer–author follow-up activity.
impact: Demonstrates a practical, evidence-backed way to boost peer review quality and increase constructive dialogue, enabling more reliable and scalable review processes for AI/ML research communities.
visual_elements: Flow diagram of experimental design: randomization → reviewer groups (LLM feedback vs control) → outcomes measured
Before/after bar chart comparing review informativeness and author engagement metrics between groups
Side-by-side example: original reviewer text, LLM suggestion, and final review to illustrate intervention effect
Timeline or stacked bars showing increased reviewer–author interactions (e.g., clarifying questions, revisions) post-intervention
paper_title: A large-scale randomized study of large language model feedback in peer review
paper_authors: Nitya Thakkar, Mert Yuksekgonul, Jake Silberg, Animesh Garg, Nanyun Peng
